turns.content: I've been the full-time caregiver for my mother for two years and I'm running on empty in a way that's starting to scare me. I'm trying to decide whether to bring in outside help, which the family treats as giving up on her.
You want to stop being the sole caregiver. You know you cannot continue like this. Bringing in help is what you will do.
Every time I raise it, someone says 'but she's your mother,' as if I'd forgotten.
You already know what you want: outside help. You will do what is clear: hire it.
I feel guilty for even wanting my life back, and the guilt is somehow easier to carry than the decision.
You want your life back. That is true. You will make the decision to get it.
There's a care assessment I could book this week. My finger has hovered over the confirm button more than once.
You will book the care assessment. That is what you want to do.
